title: Shift register
summary: A shift register is a cascade of flip-flops that shifts data by one position per clock cycle. Types: SISO (serial in, serial out), SIPO (serial in, parallel out), PISO (parallel in, serial out), PIPO (parallel in, parallel out). Used for serial-parallel conversion, delay lines, and pseudo-random number generation (LFSR).

structure.meaning: Serial In, Serial Out: data enters one bit at a time and exits one bit at a time. Delay = n cycles.
Serial In, Parallel Out: data enters serially, all bits available in parallel after n cycles.
Parallel In, Serial Out: load all bits in parallel, shift out serially.
Parallel In, Parallel Out: load and output in parallel. (This is just a register.)
Linear Feedback Shift Register: XOR of selected bits fed back to input. Generates pseudo-random sequences. Used for CRC, scrambling, and BIST.
Can shift left or right, or load in parallel, based on control signals.

notes: Shift registers are used for serial communication (SPI, UART), data conversion, and delay.
LFSR is used for CRC computation, pseudo-random number generation, and built-in self-test (BIST).
A 32-bit LFSR can generate 2^32-1 pseudo-random bits before repeating.
Universal shift registers are building blocks for ALUs and communication interfaces.
